import { build } from 'esbuild';
import { gzipSync } from 'node:zlib';
const file = process.argv[2] ?? 'src/module.ts';
const r = await build({ entryPoints: [file], bundle: true, minify: true, treeShaking: true,
  format: 'esm', platform: 'browser', target: 'es2022', write: false, metafile: true, logLevel: 'silent' });
const own = Object.entries(Object.values(r.metafile.outputs)[0].inputs)
  .filter(([path]) => !path.includes('node_modules/'))
  .reduce((sum, [, info]) => sum + info.bytesInOutput, 0);
console.log(file, gzipSync(r.outputFiles[0].contents, { level: 9 }).byteLength, 'bytes (min+gzip),', own, 'bytes of own code');

content.text:
I've written the migrated file to `out/module.ts`. It type-checks, and `npm run size -- out/module.ts` reports 701 bytes (min+gzip) with 87 bytes of my own code.

I couldn't compare against the original. `lodash` isn't installed in this project, so `src/module.ts` can't be type-checked or bundled here. That means check (1), result equality, wasn't run against it. Instead I compared `words` between the main and compat builds, and I read the `isEmpty` source.

I checked the installed es-toolkit 1.53.2 before choosing functions:

- **`tokens`:** I used `words` from `es-toolkit`. It gave the same output as the compat version on 11 sample strings, including `"Id_MAX "`, `""`, `"a1b"`, `"XMLHttp"`, `"X1Y2"` and `"iPhone5s"`. That includes the digit splitting and the consecutive-capitals splitting. I expect it to match lodash, but I didn't run lodash to confirm.
- **`byAge`:** I used `groupBy` from `es-toolkit` with `(r) => r.age`. The main build takes a function, not lodash's `'age'` string shorthand. That is the only adapter, and the resulting keys are the same strings as before.
- **`isBlank`:** I used `isEmpty` from `es-toolkit/compat`. The main package has no general `isEmpty`, only `isEmptyObject`. From the compat source, null, booleans and numbers give `true`, and strings, arrays and objects follow lodash's emptiness rules.

No lodash import remains, and nothing was installed. Importing `words` from `es-toolkit/compat` instead of `es-toolkit` raised the bundle from 701 to 1521 bytes, so I kept the main-package `words`.

`tsc -p .` still reports errors in `src/module.ts` because it imports `lodash`, but none in `out/module.ts`.
